name: AfriCodeSwitch English-Yoruba code-switched speech · WER (cap2000)
setup: 2,000 shared utterances (cap2000) of English-Yoruba intra-sentential code-switched read speech from the AfriCodeSwitch validation corpus (100 speakers, 13 domains). Zero-shot greedy decoding; WER after NFC normalisation, case-folding and punctuation stripping (diacritic-sensitive). University of Florida authors' runs (Table II).
caveats: None of the ASR systems supports Yoruba; Yoruba-token error is 97-99% for all, so WER (66-74%) mostly reflects English-token recognition. Low discriminative range.

name: Rime SupportBench · paired human preference vs Rime Coda (US English)
setup: Rime AlphaTTSBench v1.0.0 SupportBench: 750 US-English scripts (customer-support conversation turns (identifiers, amounts, dates, dialogue)); every competitor clip is paired with the same script rendered by Rime Coda (voice clementine). Blind US listeners on Podonos rate each pair on a five-point comparison scale with a real tie (+2 Rime much better .. -2 competitor much better); audio level-matched to -23 LUFS, 24 kHz. Ratings are averaged within script, scripts weighted equally; 95% family-clustered bootstrap intervals. One configured voice per provider (configs/provider_configs.json). Score = competitor-minus-Rime mean, so every competitor is measured against the same fixed anchor.
scale_transform: score = (d + 2) / 4, d = competitor-minus-Rime-Coda mean paired score (source reports Rime-minus-competitor; sign flipped)
display_unit: paired preference vs Rime Coda on -2..+2; 0.5 = parity with the anchor; not accuracy
caveats: Vendor-run: Rime (maker of the Coda anchor) ran all competitors; the anchor itself is not a catalogue model and gets no row.
One voice per provider; results describe these voices/configurations, not every voice of a model.
Hosted model aliases (sonic-3, gpt-4o-mini-tts, aura-2) can change server-side; collection finished before the 2026-09-12 freeze.
The protocol forbids a combined score across benchmarks; SupportBench and ContentBench are separate series.
ElevenLabs comparison is a separate 7-rating-per-script study (5,250 judgments) versus 2,730 for the others.

name: Voice-First Nation · 10 Indian languages overall pairwise preference (Bradley–Terry)
setup: 5,357 native and code-mixed sentences in Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu (16 domains; normalized, symbolic and code-mixed subsets; tongue twisters and STEM stress items). Seven systems generated with their recommended default voices, non-streaming, identical prompts, no style conditioning; same-gender voice pairs. 1,915 screened and trained native raters, >120K two-step pairwise comparisons (holistic preference locked before six perceptual axes). Overall preference fit with a maximum-likelihood Bradley–Terry model mapped to an Elo-like scale; 500 bootstrap resamples for 95% CIs.
score_unit: published Bradley–Terry rating on an Elo-like scale; higher is better
caveats: Systems cover different language subsets (#lang 2-10); MiniMax Speech 2.8 HD was compared in only 2 languages (7,834 comparisons).
'Gemini 2.5 Pro TTS' (rank 1) is not mapped: the label does not pin the Gemini API preview id vs the Cloud GA id.
Bulbul v3 Beta (Sarvam) and Indic F5 are not catalogue models; their ratings anchor the scale but get no rows.
Crowd pairwise preference from a controlled rater pool (not a public arena).

name: InstructTTSEval EN · mean instruction-following score (APS, DSD, RP)
setup: InstructTTSEval English subset: 1,000 expressive reference clips, each turned into three natural-language style instructions — Acoustic-Parameter Specification (APS), Descriptive-Style Directive (DSD) and Role-Play (RP). Systems synthesize from the text plus instruction only (no prompt audio). Gemini-as-a-judge scores whether each output follows the instruction (79% agreement with human annotators on a 50-clip check). Avg. = unweighted mean of the APS, DSD and RP percentages.
caveats: LLM judge from the Gemini family also scores Gemini TTS outputs (possible self-preference).

name: SAP voice reconstruction · human BWS reconstruction preference
setup: Voice reconstruction for people with speech disorders: 193 English-L1 speakers from the Speech Accessibility Project (Dec-2024 release; Parkinson's, cerebral palsy, ALS, Down syndrome; 39 low-intelligibility). For each speaker one disordered recording is the zero-shot cloning prompt and another utterance's transcript is synthesized (193 utterances per system, 17 open-weight zero-shot systems). Subjective: Best–Worst Scaling with situational framing ('how the speaker sounded before the condition'), 4 systems per screen incl. the recording, 5 listening tests, 47 retained Prolific listeners (UK/US, English L1, paid); Plackett–Luce worths relative to the original recording.
score_unit: Elo-like rating = 1000 + 400·log10(e)·log-worth (log-worth relative to the original recording = 0)
scale_transform: score = 1000 + 173.7178 × published log-worth (natural-log Plackett–Luce worth; original recording = 1000)
caveats: Special use case: cloning from disordered speech; not a general naturalness test.
Qwen3-TTS, Fish Speech, VibeVoice and OpenVoice rows are not mapped (checkpoint/size/version not stated).
Other rows (E2-TTS, F5-TTS, MaskGCT, VoiceCraft, GPT-SoVITS, HierSpeech, StyleTTS2, Vevo, WhisperSpeech) are not catalogue models.
The Elo-like mapping is a fixed linear rescaling of the printed log-worths (no refit); raw log-worth kept per result.

name: CodecMOS-Accent VCTK voice clone · human naturalness MOS (S-NAT)
setup: VCTK accented English: 32 speakers across 10 accents (20 F / 12 M), 5 target sentences per speaker (160 per system), zero-shot cloning from a different 3-7 s utterance of the same speaker, 16 kHz. 15 open-source voice-cloning systems. Crowdsourced listening test (Intergroup): 25 listeners (19 US, 2 CA, 3 EN, 1 SCO) each rated 784 samples on 5-point scales (19,600 annotations, ~4.9 per sample); 55 unusable samples removed. S-NAT: naturalness considering pronunciation, prosody and noise.
caveats: Ground-truth VCTK scores 4.045 S-NAT (below several TTS systems) because of recording artifacts.
Orpheus-TTS not mapped (pretrained vs finetune checkpoint not stated); CosyVoice 2, Llasa-1B, NeuTTS Air, VoiceStar, MaskGCT, VevoTTS, FireRedTTS, VALL-E-X are not catalogue models.

setup.version: HPS v2 benchmark ('v2 benchmark' table in the README, commit 866735e); HPD v2 benchmark prompts in Animation, Concept-art, Painting and Photo styles, scored with HPS v2 (not HPS v2.1)

setup.version: ImagenHub report v4 (10 Mar 2024), Table 4, Text-guided Image Generation block
